description: The Transboundary Wetlands Database lists wetlands that cross or sit on international borders, as a reference for studying how shared wetlands are governed within international river basins. It covers 300 wetlands in more than 80 international river basins, mainly Wetlands of International Importance under the 1971 Ramsar Convention: 22 Transboundary Ramsar Sites made up of 65 individual sites designated by 26 countries, 210 individual Ramsar sites extending into one or more other countries, 12 wetlands identified as transboundary in earlier literature, 9 found by spatial analysis and 4 non-Ramsar wetlands. It is maintained by the Program in Water Conflict Management and Transformation at Oregon State University and accompanies the article by Rosenblum and Schmeier (2022) in the journal Water. The database is available as a downloadable Excel file with fields on Ramsar designation, country and region, the international basin each wetland sits in and whether a river basin organisation exists; the page read states no licence, and it is free. Caveats: it is a tabular list without boundaries, so spatial work needs Ramsar site geometries. It supports analysis of cross-border green-blue infrastructure, shared flood storage and basin governance for climate adaptation; a related record is the Lower Danube Green Corridor case study.
